speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Livelihoods are at stake and the competition will drive the industry to deliver better services to commuters.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Moreover, under dynamic pricing, it is not certain how fares will trend.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Fares can potentially be higher during peak periods, but also lower during off-peak periods.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Competition with fast-growing private hire car services will also keep fares in check.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am glad that the Minister mentioned that he needs one week's notice from the taxi operators.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is good that there are positive benefits from the surge and dynamic pricing.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But let us, say, an example of a scenario where the prices surge in one day because of a certain event or activity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What would be the implications for a needy family, for example, which needs to send a family member to a hospital for urgent treatment especially at that particular moment when there is an extreme sharp jump in prices?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Does the Ministry take that sort of situation into consideration, especially for needy families?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, even when there is surge pricing, there are other traditional options available for any family that may have an urgent need.
